newsitem.title: FRANCE: French officials deny tax system report.
newsitem.headline: French officials deny tax system report.

text.p: French officials denied on Thursday a published report that a group of European countries including France and Germany was secretly discussing plans to create a single European tax authority.

British daily The Independent reported on Thursday that an alliance of European countries including France and Germany -- but not Britain -- were "privately negotiating" such a plan as part of the transition to a single European currency.
It said the negotiations were taking place as part of an initiative to reform European Union institutions.
French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis called the report "completely false" and said there was no question of diminishing economic sovereignty.
"There is no question of breaking with fiscal sovereignty or budgetary sovereignty," he told reporters after a conference on export credits.

French European Affairs Minister Michel Barnier, a key architect of the French position in EU institutional reform talks, said he was unaware of any such proposal and ascribed the report to the British general election campaign.
"From where I sit, and I am very involved in these negotiations, I can tell you I have never heard of any such thing," he told Reuters in Aubusson, central France.

A Finance Ministry spokeswoman said any agreement on a common tax system would have to be negotiated by all 15 European Union states including Britain, where officials had said they were unaware of the plan.
The newspaper, citing "papers seen by The Independent", said the plan envisaged control over income tax being pooled by national governments inside a future single currency zone.
It said the group's intention was to make the plan a part of new European Union flexibility provisions.

But Barnier said the flexibility provisions on which France and Germany were working were primarily aimed at enabling member states which wished to work more closely in the areas of defence and foreign policy to remain sovereign on direct taxation and social security.
